title: Buckaroo Bowl III
dek: Buckaroo Bowl III was the 2025 championship game of the Buckaroo Football League, in which Sonny's top-seeded Ben Dover beat Randy's The fumblers 105.1 to 86.48 in NFL Week 18 to complete a worst-to-first run to the league's first title won by someone other than Kaushal.
body: Buckaroo Bowl III was played over NFL Week 18 of the 2025 season to decide the championship of the Buckaroo Football League, then a six-team league in its third year. It matched the No. 1 seed, Ben Dover, managed by Sonny, against the No. 2 seed, The fumblers, managed by Randy. Neither manager had won a title. The first two Buckaroo Bowls had both gone to Kaushal's Habibsters.

Ben Dover finished the regular season 13-3 with a league-best 1,850.8 points, about 115.7 per game. The record stood out because of Sonny's history: Ben Dover had finished last in both 2023 and 2024. The fumblers went 9-7 and scored 1,792.1 points, about 112.0 per game, 58.7 fewer than Ben Dover over the season.

The teams met twice in the regular season, and Ben Dover won both games easily. Sonny took Week 5 118.84 to 88.32 and Week 10 153.42 to 97.9, outscoring Randy 272.26 to 186.22 across the two meetings. Luffy still made The fumblers the favorite, giving Randy a 59 percent title chance to Sonny's 41 percent. The projections explained the call: Randy's starting lineup was projected for 117.8 points and Sonny's for 110.8.

The fumblers reached the final through a Week 17 playoff game against Habibsters, which ended Kaushal's bid for a third straight Buckaroo Bowl. Randy won 137.1 to 79.96, a margin of 57.14 points. Derrick Henry carried the game with 45.6 points, one of the biggest single-game performances of the Buckaroo postseason.

Ben Dover reached the final as the top seed on the strength of its 13-3 regular season and the league's highest point total. Sonny came into the championship having beaten his opponent twice by a combined 86.04 points. That gave the matchup a familiar feel despite Luffy's lean the other way.

Trevor Lawrence set the tone early. Making his first start for Ben Dover, the Jacksonville quarterback threw a 23-yard touchdown to Parker Washington in the first quarter against Tennessee. He added two more in the second quarter, a 7-yarder to Brenton Strange and a 5-yarder to Quintin Morris. Three first-half touchdown passes gave Sonny the biggest single source of points either team would get all week.

The fumblers answered mostly through special teams and defense. In the first quarter of Los Angeles at Denver, Ja'Quan McMillian returned an interception 45 yards for a touchdown, and the Broncos D/ST finished with 20 points, the highest total on either roster. Harrison Mevis, also making his first start for Randy, kicked field goals of 34, 42 and 40 yards in the first half of Arizona at Los Angeles. Mevis finished with 15 points.

Randy's Bears-heavy lineup waited until late in Detroit at Chicago. In the fourth quarter, Caleb Williams threw a 25-yard touchdown to Jahdae Walker, converted with a Kyle Monangai run, and then a 1-yard touchdown to Colston Loveland, adding a two-point pass to Cole Kmet. The rally gave Williams 16.6 points but could not cover the gaps elsewhere in the lineup. On Ben Dover's side, Jason Myers added field goals of 45 yards in the second quarter and 31 yards in the fourth of Seattle at San Francisco for 6 points.
Ben Dover's 105.1 points were 5.7 below projection, but The fumblers fell 31.32 short of theirs. The final margin was 18.6 points. Sonny's win made Luffy's 59 percent favorite the runner-up.

Lawrence led Ben Dover with 23.3 points against a 21.5 projection. Kenneth Walker III scored 15.3, well above his 10.6 projection and his 9.0 average across three earlier starts for the team. Justin Jefferson added 14.4 against an 11.8 projection, beating his season average of 9.5 per start. The Patriots D/ST more than doubled its projection with 14 points, and Sonny's choice to start it over the Seahawks D/ST (12 points on the bench) turned out right.

Not everything worked for Ben Dover. Trey McBride, the team's most reliable scorer at 15.2 points per start, managed 10. George Kittle scored 5.4 against an 11.8 projection, and Stefon Diggs scored 5.8 against the same projection. Ashton Jeanty finished with 10.9, short of his 14.3 projection.

For The fumblers, the Broncos D/ST (20 points against a 7.5 projection) and Mevis (15 against 9.3) were the bright spots. The skill positions mostly failed. James Cook III, who had averaged 18.4 points over 15 starts, scored 1.5 against a 19.3 projection. George Pickens scored 1.4 against a 13.3 projection after averaging 15.3 per start. D'Andre Swift managed 5.3 against a 14.0 projection, and Derrick Henry followed his 45.6-point semifinal with 12.6.

The bench decided the story. Randy left Detroit's Amon-Ra St. Brown on the bench with 19.4 points while starting Bears receiver Luther Burden III (6.0) in the same game. Starting St. Brown over Pickens alone would have left The fumblers 0.62 points short. Pairing that move with Deebo Samuel's 3.1 bench points in place of Cook's 1.5 would have given Randy a 106.08 total and the title by 0.98.

The win gave Sonny his first Buckaroo Bowl and made him the first champion other than Kaushal. It completed one of the sharpest turnarounds in league history: two straight last-place finishes, followed by a 13-3 regular season, the top seed and a title. The commissioner who had built the league finally had his name on its trophy.

Randy finished second of six, the best result of his Buckaroo career to that point. His runner-up season will be remembered for both regular-season losses to the champion and the 19.4 points left on his bench in the final. At the other end of the 2025 standings, the consolation ladder sent last place to Mekhi's Dawgs, ending Ben Dover's two-year hold on the spot.

The league expanded to eight teams for 2026, and Sonny renamed his team The Horse is Hea. Buckaroo Bowl III was the last championship of the six-team era, and the defending champion entered the new format carrying a worst-to-first story no other manager could claim.
